The term `` gymnosperm '' comes from the Greek composite word γυμνόσπερμος
γυμνός gymnos , `` naked ''
σπέρμα sperma , `` seed ''
The term `` gymnosperm '' comes from the Greek composite word γυμνόσπερμος ( γυμνός gymnos , `` naked '' and σπέρμα sperma , `` seed '' ) , meaning `` naked seeds ''
The name is based on the unenclosed condition of their seeds
The name is based on the unenclosed condition of their seeds ( called ovules in their unfertilized state )
The non-encased condition of their seeds stands in contrast to the seeds and ovules of flowering plants ( angiosperms ) , which are enclosed within an ovary

Gymnosperm seeds develop either on the surface of scales or leaves
